messages:
maya: quick heads-up — while testing speculative decoding on the quantized 13B bring-up (q4_0), I saw an oscillatory quality regression across seeds. runs look fast but accept rate dips intermittently.

sam: can you paste the command you ran and the exact metrics?

maya: ran the usual harness: `./run_eval.sh --model redwood-13b-q4_0 --decoder speculative --spec-config spec_v3.json --seed $SEED --suite redwood-eval-suite-v2`

maya: perf: 2.8x token throughput vs greedy. latency median 120ms -> 42ms with spec. but acceptance_rate (our human proxy) jumped from 92% -> 86% for some seeds.

liam: interesting. oscillatory as in sometimes it's fine, sometimes it regresses?

maya: exactly. same commit, same env, different seeds. seed 42 was OK, seed 7 had a clear drop. variance much larger than quantization-only runs.

ciara: could be sampling randomness interacting with quantization noise + speculative prefetch ordering. did you try deterministic sampling (topk with fixed rng)?

maya: tried `--seed` and `--temperature 0.0` (argmax) — then speculative is moot (no branching) and quality matches baseline. the issue only shows with stochastic decode (temp=0.8 / top-p 0.9).

ashley: any logs from the runtime? e.g., prefetch misses, fallback counts, kv-cache evictions?

maya: pasted excerpt:

```
[spec_runtime] prefix_prefetch_hit: 0.71
[spec_runtime] fallback_to_decoder: 0.08
[spec_runtime] speculative_misfire_rate: 0.042
[kv] evictions: 0
```

maya: misfire_rate correlates with lower acceptance. when misfire spikes we see odd token choices.

sam: ok. could be that quantization reduces confidence gaps between top tokens, so speculative predictor is overconfident on wrong token. do we have top-k logits distance distribution?

liam: I pulled logit gap histograms earlier — quant q4 shows narrower argmax margins across many positions vs fp16. attaching snippet in thread.

ciara: if predictor threshold tuned on fp16, it might be too aggressive on q4. try raising the threshold or using conservative fallback policy for quant models.

maya: tried bumping predictor threshold from 0.7 -> 0.85; misfire down to 0.017 and acceptance_rate back to 90.5%, throughput still 2.1x.

ashley: that's promising. are we confident this generalizes across prompts? maybe the threshold tuning overfits the eval suite.

maya: ran on holdout prompt set (dev_holdout_1k). results consistent but more noise. still seeing seed sensitivity for extreme prompts (lots of named entities).

ciara: suggestion: add a lightweight calibration pass per model that computes logistic map from logit-gap to success probability and set threshold to target p>0.98. run during onboarding.

liam: agree. also add a jittered-seed sweep to quantify worst-case drop; generate 10 seeds and report min acceptance along with median. current single-seed reports hide tail regressions.

sam: for rollout: canary 2% with baseline fallback policy (threshold conservative) and realtime eval-bot scoring on user-allowed prompts. if acceptance dips >2% vs baseline, auto-roll back.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary 2% at 2026-04-02T18:00Z, policy conservative-spec-v1 applied.

maya: one more oddity — sometimes speculative path introduces short-range ngram repeats in q4 that I didn't see in fp16. looks like lattice collapse in two-step speculative acceptance. logging examples: `"...the the system"` appears more.

ciara: that feels like predictor picking token that later sampling prefers to repeat. we should add a repeat-penalty heuristic in the speculative accept stage (cheap check).

ashley: action items: (1) implement calibration pass and threshold tuning in onboarding (owner: ciara), (2) add jittered-seed sweep to eval harness and surface worst-case (owner: liam), (3) short repeat-penalty in speculative accept (owner: ashley), (4) canary rollout with eval-bot guard (owner: sam).

maya: added to board and started PR for logging hooks. thanks all. :thumbsup:

eval-bot: eval run queued: redwood-13b-q4_0 spec_v3 calibration-sweep x10 seeds. link: https://ci.redwood/evals/2812345678

sam: let's reconvene after the calibration sweep results. short sync tomorrow 10:30am PT.

maya: noted. I'll upload the failing example set in a gist for manual inspection.

liam: nice triage. keeping the conservative default for Dedicated customers too.

maya: done — gist link pasted in eval thread.
